concepts.definition: Constitutional typed contract law for graph-native programs, with inspectable and traceable authoring validity, diagnostics, repair affordances, declarations-as-data and conformance corpus truth.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-001**: GTL shall be the constitutional typed
contract-law API for graph-native programs. Authoring validity, diagnostics,
repair affordances, declarations-as-data, and conformance corpus truth shall be
inspectable and traceable.

concepts.label: GTL contract-law API

concepts.definition: Declaration owner of topology, starts, GraphFunction membership, compute composition, policy, effects, results and proof obligations; neither runtime plan nor callable function.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-003**: A GTL program shall own topology, starts,
GraphFunction membership, compute composition, policy, effects, results, and
proof obligations. A program is not a runtime plan or callable function.

concepts.label: GTL program

concepts.definition: Sole public named callable work contract and primary reusable workflow-library compute abstraction: a typed outer interface plus replayable GTL template materializing a graph.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-004**: GraphFunction shall be the sole public
named callable work contract. It shall publish a typed outer interface and
replayable GTL template that materializes a graph. An implementation binding
shall not replace that constructive body.

Define `GraphFunction` as the primary reusable GTL workflow-library compute
abstraction and contract boundary for lawful workflow reuse.

concepts.label: GraphFunction

concepts.definition: Language-owned immutable structural topology/materialization value composed of nodes, vectors, contexts, rules, effects and boundary nodes; structure alone is not a callable workflow or semantic job target.

grounding.quote:
Define `Graph` as the first-class structural topology and materialization surface
of GTL 3.

`Graph` is the language-owned structure made of nodes, graph vectors, contexts,
rules, effects, and boundary nodes. It is not the public callable workflow
carrier by itself. Public work entry and semantic jobs bind through published
`GraphFunction` carriers that materialize graph structure.
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPH-001**: `Graph` shall be a frozen, immutable value type with at minimum: `id`, `name`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `nodes`, `vectors`, `contexts`, `rules`, `effects`, and `tags`.

concepts.label: Graph

concepts.definition: First-class immutable GTL convergence, attestation and gate-assessment declaration with at least name, regime, description, binding and tags; asks whether contracts, outputs or gates satisfy their declared criteria.

grounding.quote:
Define evaluators as first-class GTL declarations for convergence, attestation,
and gate-visible assessment.

**REQ-L-GTL3-EVALUATOR-001**: `Evaluator` shall be a frozen, immutable declaration type with at minimum: `name`, `regime`, `description`, `binding`, and `tags`.

**REQ-L-GTL3-EVALUATOR-002**: Evaluators answer convergence questions such as whether a contract is satisfied, an output has converged, or a gate has passed.

concepts.label: Evaluator

concepts.definition: Planned substitution of one admitted refinement GraphFunction into one exact GraphVector of an admitted parent, selected by declared refinement, candidate-family or published traversal-target authority.

grounding.quote:
Define the published GraphFunction refinement declarations that close the
language boundary for zoom, recursive foldback, and typed composition. These
are GTL program laws. HoG traverses their admitted structure and ABG admits
their runtime consequences; neither invents their structural meaning.

**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPHFUNCTION-REFINEMENT-001**: GraphFunction zoom shall be a
planned substitution of one admitted refinement GraphFunction into one exact
GraphVector of an admitted parent GraphFunction. The selected vector shall be
grounded by at least one declared `RefinementBoundary`, `CandidateFamily`, or
published traversal-target reference. Zero or multiple matches shall fail
admission or construction; names, ordinals, or ambient runtime state shall not
select the target.

concepts.label: GraphFunction zoom plan

concepts.definition: Declared rebind of child completion into a parent with one nonempty binding and mandatory parent re-evaluation; child completion is input, never parent certification.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPHFUNCTION-REFINEMENT-003**: Recursive GraphFunction foldback
shall declare `rebind` mode, one non-empty binding, and mandatory parent
re-evaluation. Child completion supplies rebind input; it shall not certify the
parent or bypass its evaluator. Additional foldback attributes are inert
declaration data unless admitted by an owning requirement.

concepts.label: Recursive foldback declaration

concepts.definition: Explicit left provided/carry node to right required node wiring under one published node-type declaration reference, preserving schema, Markov and asset-surface obligations.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPHFUNCTION-REFINEMENT-004**: Typed GraphFunction composition
shall name a left provided/carry node, a right required node, and one published
node-type declaration reference for every wiring. Both nodes shall satisfy that
same node type without weakening schema, Markov, or asset-surface law. Missing
nodes, unknown or non-node-type declaration references, incompatible
contracts, or an empty wiring set shall fail before composition.

concepts.label: GraphFunction type wiring

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-002**: Core graph algebra shall remain
`edge`, `compose`, `substitute`, `recurse`, `fan_out`, `fan_in`,
`gate`, `promote`, `identity`, and `same_object`. Host spellings may
vary only when carrier identity and law are preserved.

**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-005**: The seven C constructors and selected
`F_D`, `F_P`, and `F_H` composition shall be typed, inspectable GTL
declaration truth. Compute regimes shall not exchange authority.

constraints.statement: Core graph algebra remains edge, compose, substitute, recurse, fan_out, fan_in, gate, promote, identity and same_object. The seven C constructors and F_D/F_P/F_H selection remain typed inspectable declaration truth with no authority exchange between regimes.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-004**: GraphFunction shall be the sole public
named callable work contract. It shall publish a typed outer interface and
replayable GTL template that materializes a graph. An implementation binding
shall not replace that constructive body.

**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-005**: The seven C constructors and selected
`F_D`, `F_P`, and `F_H` composition shall be typed, inspectable GTL
declaration truth. Compute regimes shall not exchange authority.

**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-006**: Recursive GraphFunctions shall declare
the callable relation, termination, foldback, lineage, and bounds. HoG shall
traverse the declared relation; ABG shall admit child and parent runtime truth.
No hidden recursive controller is permitted.

constraints.statement: Publish the typed outer interface and replayable graph-materializing GTL template; implementation bindings may not replace the constructive body. Recursive functions declare callable relation, termination, foldback, lineage and bounds; HoG traverses that relation and ABG admits child/parent runtime truth, with no hidden recursion controller.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-007**: Plugin, worker, handler, tool, and native
function bindings shall identify only declared implementation seams, input and
output contracts, compute means, capability requirements, and authority
denials. They shall not own topology, traversal, events, continuation, or
closure.

constraints.statement: Plugin, Worker, handler, tool and native bindings identify only declared seams, I/O contracts, compute means, capability requirements and authority denials. They never own topology, traversal, events, continuation or closure.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-008**: Prompt construction and other typed assets
shall be declared through GTL asset contracts with constructor, renderer,
digest, authority slot, output contract, proof, node, and evidence relations.
Rendered text is not authority.

constraints.statement: Prompt construction and other typed assets use GTL contracts with constructor, renderer, digest, authority-slot, output-contract, proof, node and evidence relations. Rendered text is not authority.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-009**: One deterministic GTL validator shall
apply native-equivalent law to serialized programs and shall report typed
validity, invalidity, or unresolved semantics. It may produce canonical
serialization and subordinate indexes but shall not produce an executable
program or runtime truth.

**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-016**: The GTL validator shall project declared
entry, internal vector, start-to-entry, program-membership, implementation-seam,
output-admission, consequence, and catalog-bind relations without executing
them. Missing, ambiguous, illegal, or incomplete relations shall remain typed
non-conformance.

constraints.statement: One deterministic GTL validator applies native-equivalent law to serialized programs and reports typed validity, invalidity or unresolved semantics. Canonical serialization and subordinate indexes are allowed, executable programs and runtime truth are not. It projects declared entry, vector, start-entry, membership, seam, output-admission, consequence and catalog-bind relations without executing them; missing, ambiguous, illegal or incomplete relations remain typed nonconformance.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-010**: HoG shall traverse the original admitted
GTL program and materialized GraphFunction graphs directly. A generated HoG
program, CompiledCProgramPlan, compiled execution declaration, ladder, or
runtime-program catalog shall fail as executable authority.

**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-011**: ABG shall own admission, graph-call and
frame identity, effects and result truth, events, replay, evidence, correction,
continuation, and closure around HoG traversal. ABG shall not redefine GTL
program meaning.

constraints.statement: HoG directly traverses original admitted GTL and materialized GraphFunction graphs. Generated HoG programs, CompiledCProgramPlan, compiled execution declarations, ladders and runtime-program catalogs fail as executable authority. ABG owns admission, graph-call/frame identity, effects/result truth, events, replay, evidence, correction, continuation and closure around traversal, without redefining GTL meaning.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-012**: Downstream products shall not create
second contract-law, validator, executor, event, replay, continuation, or
closure surfaces in parsers, prompt prose, adapters, plugins, fixtures, or
generated read models.

**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-013**: Every concrete authoring or serialized
carrier accepted by a build tenant shall trace to a GTL declaration, GTL
validator rule, or ABG runtime-admission contract.

constraints.statement: Downstream parsers, prompt prose, adapters, plugins, fixtures and generated read models may not create second contract-law, validator, executor, event, replay, continuation or closure surfaces. Every accepted concrete authored/serialized carrier traces to a GTL declaration, GTL validator rule or ABG runtime-admission contract.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-015**: `PRODUCT.md`,
`requirements/gtl/README.md`, and installed context projections shall
identify this file as the fast reload surface and shall bind enough identity to
detect stale versions.

**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-016**: The GTL validator shall project declared
entry, internal vector, start-to-entry, program-membership, implementation-seam,
output-admission, consequence, and catalog-bind relations without executing
them. Missing, ambiguous, illegal, or incomplete relations shall remain typed
non-conformance.

**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-017**: Validation shall expose the declared
conservation basis for every traversal bind, including intent lineage, target
carriers, materialization authority, carried obligations, residual pressure,
allowed dispositions, admission strength, and obligation delta. Missing
conservation law blocks traversal admission.

constraints.statement: PRODUCT.md, GTL README and installed context projections identify this fast reload file with identity sufficient to detect staleness. Validation exposes conservation basis for every traversal bind: intent lineage, target carriers, materialization authority, obligations, residual pressure, dispositions, admission strength and obligation delta. Missing conservation law blocks traversal admission.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-CONTRACT-LAW-API-018**: Requirement, traversal-span, context,
destination-topology, test-relation, and evidence-policy declarations shall use
existing GTL publication and attachment law. They feed ABG admission and replay
but shall not emit events, write ledgers, select traversal, or close work.

constraints.statement: Requirement, traversal-span, context, destination-topology, test-relation and evidence-policy declarations use existing publication/attachment law. They feed admission/replay but cannot emit events, write ledgers, select traversal or close work.

grounding.quote:
| Question | Declaration owner | Validation | Execution and truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| program topology and starts | GTL program | GTL validator | HoG traverses; ABG admits |
| named callable work | GraphFunction template and contracts | GTL validator | HoG traverses materialized graph |
| local transition | GraphVector | GTL validator | HoG advances locus; ABG records |
| compute interior | C plus F_D/F_P/F_H declaration | GTL validator | implementation performs; ABG admits |
| recursion and refinement | GTL GraphFunction relation | GTL validator | HoG child frame; ABG foldback truth |
| runtime effects and results | declared implementation seam | admission contract | implementation acts; ABG admits |
| continuation and closure | GTL policy and result contracts | validator plus admission | ABG replay-derived state |
| downstream domain meaning | downstream Product and Module | common contract law | common HoG and ABG path |

constraints.statement: The declared router assigns topology/starts to GTL Program, callable work to GraphFunction templates/contracts, local transitions to GraphVector, compute interiors to C/regimes, recursion/refinement to GraphFunction relations, effects/results to seams, continuation/closure to GTL policy/result contracts, and domain meaning to downstream Product/Module. GTL validates structure and common law; admission validates effects/results and joins continuation/closure checks. HoG traverses/advances admitted structures, implementations act within interiors, and ABG admits runtime truth, records loci, admits foldback and supplies replay-derived continuation/closure. All downstream work uses the common HoG/ABG path.

grounding.quote:
Types, lints, validator reports, package manifests, operation counts, catalog
rows, event co-presence, and generated documentation are necessary evidence
where applicable. None substitutes for the installed causal path or for the
complete Product scenarios.

constraints.statement: Types, lint, reports, package manifests, counts, catalog rows, event co-presence and generated documentation are necessary where applicable, but none substitutes for the installed causal path or complete Product scenarios.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-EVALUATOR-004**: Evaluator `binding` shall be a declared implementation reference resolved by an engine or plugin. GTL declares the evaluator; engines provide executable realization and provenance.

**REQ-L-GTL3-EVALUATOR-005**: Evaluator multiplicity and ordering may be declared at a contract boundary without embedding domain closure semantics in the interpreter.

**REQ-L-GTL3-EVALUATOR-006**: Domain-specific gap, closure, ranking, or attestation semantics belong to evaluator declarations and their resolved implementations, not to the interpreter.

constraints.statement: Binding is a declared implementation reference resolved by engine/plugin: GTL owns declaration and engines supply executable realization and provenance. Domain gap, closure, ranking and attestation semantics belong to the declaration and resolved implementation, never the interpreter.

conditions: Probabilistic evaluator participates in a declared edge assurance contract.

grounding.quote: **REQ-L-GTL3-EVALUATOR-007**: Probabilistic evaluator output for a declared edge assurance contract shall be a constrained finding over gain, close disposition, residual pressure, continuation, evidence, authority, and composition refs. Such output shall not directly close the edge, write a ledger, select a vector, or emit runtime events. If F_P proposes human involvement, that proposed close disposition shall be distinct from ABG's F_H-by-absentia disposition for a missing edge assurance contract.

constraints.statement: F_P output under an edge assurance contract is a constrained finding over gain, close disposition, residual pressure, continuation, evidence, authority and composition references. It cannot directly close, write ledgers, select vectors or emit events. Proposed human involvement is a distinct close disposition from ABG F_H-by-absentia for a missing edge assurance contract.

grounding.quote: **REQ-L-GTL3-EVALUATOR-008**: Evaluator declarations that participate in an `abg.fn_composition` contract shall preserve the evaluator regime, role, authority, consumed field refs, input carrier refs, output carrier refs, and evidence refs needed by ABG admission. A probabilistic or human evaluator may emit evidence or judgment state under the selected composition identity, but it shall not claim deterministic closure authority.

constraints.statement: Composition-participating evaluators preserve regime, role, authority, consumed fields, input/output carrier and evidence references needed by ABG admission. F_P/F_H may emit evidence or judgment under selected composition identity, never deterministic closure authority.

conditions: Authority placement depends on consumed output fields.
exceptions: Empty consumedFieldRefs is lawful only without such field-local consumption.

grounding.quote: **REQ-L-GTL3-EVALUATOR-009**: Evaluator declarations shall expose `consumedFieldRefs` as an admitted carrier field when deterministic authority placement depends on which output fields downstream routing, execution construction, pressure projection, or closure predicates read. An empty consumed-field set is lawful only when the evaluator does not consume field-local payload truth for those decisions.

constraints.statement: When deterministic authority placement depends on output fields read by routing, execution construction, pressure projection or closure predicates, expose consumedFieldRefs as an admitted carrier field. An empty set is lawful only if no field-local payload truth is consumed for those decisions.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPH-001**: `Graph` shall be a frozen, immutable value type with at minimum: `id`, `name`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `nodes`, `vectors`, `contexts`, `rules`, `effects`, and `tags`.

**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPH-002**: A primitive graph step shall be representable as a minimal `Graph`. GTL shall not require a rival structural ontology for single-step workflows.

**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPH-003**: A multi-step workflow, refined workflow, composed workflow, recursive workflow, and higher-order workflow shall all be expressible as `Graph`.

**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPH-004**: `Graph` shall declare its boundary interface through designated input and output nodes.
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPH-006**: `Graph` shall carry local constraints and declared or derived execution-regime visibility through `rules` and `effects`.

constraints.statement: Graph is frozen/immutable with at least id, name, inputs, outputs, nodes, vectors, contexts, rules, effects and tags. Minimal single-step, multistep, refined, composed, recursive and higher-order workflows are all Graph-expressible without a rival single-step ontology. Inputs/outputs are designated boundary nodes; rules/effects carry constraints and declared/derived regime visibility.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPH-005**: `Graph` shall be the unit of substitution and composition at the structural level. This structural composition role shall not make `Graph` a public callable workflow carrier or semantic job target.

**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPH-006**: `Graph` shall carry local constraints and declared or derived execution-regime visibility through `rules` and `effects`.

**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPH-007**: A `Graph` may be materialized by a published `GraphFunction`, but the `GraphFunction` shall remain the reusable workflow-library function and public callable carrier.

**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPH-008**: Public execution shall follow the current GTL/ABG chain: `Job` -> `GraphFunction` -> ABG `GraphCall` -> materialized `Graph` -> internal `GraphVector` traversal. `Graph` shall not be targeted as a bare public execution entrypoint.

**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPH-009**: Product-local terms such as graph overlay, workflow lane, app surface, or lifecycle graph may be used only when they bind back to `Graph`, `GraphFunction`, `Job`, or another first-class GTL declaration surface before declaring GTL or ABG behavior.

constraints.statement: Graph is structural substitution/composition unit, not callable work or semantic Job target. Published GraphFunction may materialize it and remains the reusable callable. Public chain is Job -> GraphFunction -> ABG GraphCall -> materialized Graph -> internal GraphVector traversal, never bare Graph execution. Product terms such as overlay/lane/app surface/lifecycle graph must bind back to first-class GTL carriers before claiming GTL/ABG behavior.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPHFUNCTION-REFINEMENT-001**: GraphFunction zoom shall be a
planned substitution of one admitted refinement GraphFunction into one exact
GraphVector of an admitted parent GraphFunction. The selected vector shall be
grounded by at least one declared `RefinementBoundary`, `CandidateFamily`, or
published traversal-target reference. Zero or multiple matches shall fail
admission or construction; names, ordinals, or ambient runtime state shall not
select the target.

constraints.statement: Select exactly one parent vector by at least one declared RefinementBoundary, CandidateFamily or published traversal-target reference. Zero or multiple matches fail admission/construction; names, ordinals and ambient runtime state cannot select targets.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPHFUNCTION-REFINEMENT-002**: A zoom plan shall bind the parent
GraphFunction and graph identities, target GraphVector identity and interface,
refinement GraphFunction and graph identities, substituted graph identity, and
all selecting authority references. Application shall reject drift in any
bound identity. The resulting GraphFunction shall preserve the parent's
declared input and output interface and publish the plan as declaration data.

constraints.statement: Bind parent function/graph, vector identity/interface, refinement function/graph, substituted graph identity and all selecting authority references. Reject drift in any bound identity. Preserve parent input/output interface and publish the plan as declaration data.

exceptions: An owning requirement may admit semantics for extra foldback attributes.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPHFUNCTION-REFINEMENT-003**: Recursive GraphFunction foldback
shall declare `rebind` mode, one non-empty binding, and mandatory parent
re-evaluation. Child completion supplies rebind input; it shall not certify the
parent or bypass its evaluator. Additional foldback attributes are inert
declaration data unless admitted by an owning requirement.

constraints.statement: Declare rebind mode, exactly one nonempty binding and mandatory parent re-evaluation. Child completion supplies rebind input, not certification or evaluator bypass. Extra attributes are inert unless an owning requirement admits their semantics.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPHFUNCTION-REFINEMENT-004**: Typed GraphFunction composition
shall name a left provided/carry node, a right required node, and one published
node-type declaration reference for every wiring. Both nodes shall satisfy that
same node type without weakening schema, Markov, or asset-surface law. Missing
nodes, unknown or non-node-type declaration references, incompatible
contracts, or an empty wiring set shall fail before composition.

constraints.statement: Each wiring names the left carried/provided node, right required node and one published node-type reference. Both satisfy the same type without weakening schema, Markov or AssetSurface law. Missing nodes, unknown/non-node-type references, incompatibility and empty wiring fail before composition.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPHFUNCTION-REFINEMENT-005**: Successful typed wiring shall
produce ordinary GraphFunction composition after replacing only the declared
right-side requirement with the satisfying left-side carried node. It shall
not introduce implicit coercion, a rival edge, a runtime router, or a second
type system.

constraints.statement: Success yields ordinary GraphFunction composition after replacing only the declared right requirement with its satisfying left carried node. It adds no coercion, rival edge, runtime router or second type system.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-GRAPHFUNCTION-REFINEMENT-006**: Published host tenants shall expose
typed interfaces for zoom plans, foldback declarations, and type wiring, plus
raw admission and semantic diagnostics for serialized declarations. Native
type matching shall carry all constraints it can express; malformed or
unresolved serialized GTL shall fail at admission or GTL validation before
HoG traversal.

GTL owns the structural declarations and pure construction result. HoG owns
direct traversal of the admitted GTL structure. ABG owns runtime frames,
lineage, foldback and parent-result admission, events, replay, and closure.
Product-local dispatch or vector classification is not part of this
capability.

constraints.statement: Published tenants expose typed zoom/foldback/wiring interfaces plus raw admission and semantic diagnostics. Native types enforce everything expressible; malformed or unresolved serialized GTL fails admission/validation before HoG traversal. GTL owns declaration/pure construction, HoG direct traversal, ABG runtime frames/lineage/foldback/parent results/events/replay/closure. Product-local dispatch/vector classification is outside this capability.
